newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Trinidad says tensions eased with Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad says tensions eased with Venezuela.

text.p: Trinidad and Tobago's Prime Minister Basdeo Panday said on Wednesday he and Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera and made progress in easing tensions between their countries.
They met on Tuesday in Venezuela following several incidents in the Gulf of Paria, where both countries have oil rigs, he told Reuters.
Panday said both countries agreed there should be no more violence in the gulf and no coast guard boarding of oil rigs.
Panday and Caldera agreed to establish a special bilateral commission to investigate the raiding of a Trinidad oil rig by the Venezuelan National Guard in the Paria Gulf three weeks ago.

The rig was in Trinidad's territorial waters, Foreign Affairs Minister Ralph Maraj said. He described the action as "an incursion in Trinidad's territorial waters and a violation of this country's sovereignty."
Panday said the commission would also probe the shooting of a local trawler captain late last year by a Venezuelan military gunboat.
The commission has a month to report its findings on both incidents.
Panday said the two leaders also agreed to expedite negotiations for a new fishing agreement. The last accord expired in December.

He said the Venezuelan government indicated it would not permit fishing in certain zones because it planned to embark on drilling activities in those areas,and the presence of fishing vessels, even its own, would disturb that activity.
Caldera hoped to visit Trinidad later this year, Panday said.
The Gulf of Paria separates both countries by seven miles (11 km) at the closest point and has been the scene of frequent conflicts involving fishermen. Its waters teem with fish and shrimp.
Several Trinidad fishermen are being held in Venezuelan jails after being detained for allegedly entering that country's waters, Toy Ali, president of the Cedros Fishing Association, said.
Maraj told a local radio station that efforts are being made to free the men. He also warned trawlers operators to keep out of Venezuelan waters until a new fishing agreement was signed.
